title: Model route creation — UX playback and microcopy options
content:
Purpose:
Quick notes + annotated wireframe playback for the new model route/endpoint creation flow. Focus: make pinning and version choices explicit, reduce accidental pin-locks, and provide clear rollback/canary language. This is a working doc for sprint grooming and copy experiments.

Audience:
- PMs: product-console
- Designers: Lena (lead)
- Eng: serving-runtime + backend route service
- Solutions/SE: anyone who needs predictable defaults for customer demos

Summary / goals (short):
- Surface model variant differences early (latency/cost/quality tags)
- Make "pin to model version" an explicit, reversible action with clear consequences
- Add a canary slider for % traffic + automatic fallback option
- Include contextual microcopy and one-click suggestions for common cases (dev/test/prod)

Wireframe playback (step-by-step annotations):
1) Create route landing (card list)
   - Top bar: name, route type selector (question: route vs endpoint nomenclature)
   - CTA: "New model route" (primary)
   - Inline helper: short line: "Routes map requests to model variants and rollout policies."

2) Step 1 — Choose model
   - List view with cards: model name, variant tag (quantized/FP16), sample latency (p50/p95), cost estimate per 1k tokens, recommended workloads (chat/generation/embeddings)
   - Lightweight filters: region, latency tier, cost bracket, certified/open-source
   - Wireframe note: hovering a card reveals a small "Compare" checkbox and a quick link to run a sample prompt.

3) Step 2 — Choose variant & pin toggle (focus of this doc)
   - Variant rows: each variant shows version id, created date, commit message snippet (if available), profile badges (fast/cheap/accurate).
   - Primary control: radio select to choose active variant.
   - Pin toggle (icon + label). Default OFF. When ON we show a small banner: "Pinned — traffic will not automatically switch to newer variants".
   - Copy + options (see microcopy section).
   - Safety affordance: pin requires typing the version suffix or toggling an opt-in confirm: "Type 'PIN' to confirm" for production routes (configurable by org). This can be disabled for dev routes.

4) Step 3 — Rollout policy / traffic split
   - Canary slider (0–100%) to route X% to the selected variant.
   - Secondary dropdown: fallback variant if primary is unavailable (auto-fallback = enabled by default).
   - Button: "Save draft" / "Create route" (primary)

5) Confirmation and post-create state
   - If pinned: show prominent header pill: "Pinned to v3.1 — no auto-updates" with secondary button "Open rollback" and tertiary "Start canary".
   - If not pinned: header pill: "Following latest compatible variant" with small link to "Pin this route".

Microcopy experiments (variants to A/B test):
- Pin toggle label options:
  1) "Pin to this version (no auto-updates)"
  2) "Freeze on vX — I will manage upgrades"
  3) "Lock version — prevent automatic swaps"

- Pin confirmation dialog copy (3 options):
  A) Title: "Pin route to v3.1?" Body: "This route will keep using v3.1 until you unpin. Newer compatible model versions will not be applied automatically. You can still roll out a new version manually." CTA: "Pin now"
  B) Title: "Make this route stable" Body: "Pinning gives you predictable inference behavior. We recommend pinning for production traffic. You can enable canaries to test updates." CTA: "Confirm pin"
  C) Title: "Prevent automatic updates?" Body: "If pinned, this route will not adopt automatic upgrades. You can configure auto-rollout policies later." CTA: "Yes, pin it"

- Hover helper (on pin toggle):
  - Short: "Prevent automatic model upgrades for this route."
  - Longer: "Pinning preserves behavior but increases maintenance. We’ll show security/bugfix notes for later versions so you can decide when to upgrade."

- Canary UI copy examples:
  - Small label next to slider: "Canary — route X% to candidate; remaining traffic uses fallback/default."
  - Tooltip: "We’ll monitor latency and error regressions during the canary. If thresholds trigger, traffic will shift back to fallback."

Error states / edge copy:
- If user tries to create a pinned route without setting fallback: "We recommend a fallback model for pinned routes. Proceed without fallback?" CTA: "Create anyway" / "Add fallback"
- If a pinned model becomes incompatible with incoming requests: banner copy: "Pinned model is failing to serve some requests. Traffic is routed to fallback. Investigate v3.1 logs."
- If auto-fallback disabled and pinned fails: "Pinned route is degraded and has no fallback. Incoming requests will return 503. Enable fallback or unpin to restore service."

Acceptance criteria (for a minimal first pass):
- Designers supply final annotated wires for: choose-model list, variant selection, pin toggle dialog, canary slider, route summary header. (Lena)
- Backend: endpoint creation API accepts (model_id, variant_id, pin:boolean, canary_pct:int, fallback_variant_id). API returns route_id and status. (Eng)
- Console: visual header pill for pinned/unpinned and one-click unpin with confirmation. (Console eng)
- Tests: E2E flows for create->canary->promote->rollback. (SRE/QA)

Backlog grooming items (ordered + rough estimates):
- RED-3371 — wireframes: final annotated assets (3d) — owner: Lena — est: 2d — priority: P0
- RED-3382 — pin confirmation modal + analytics event (3pts) — owner: Marina — est: 3d — depends: backend API
- RED-3420 — add canary slider + metric hooks (5pts) — owner: Marcus — est: 1 sprint
- RED-3445 — fallback selector + validation in route create API (3pts) — owner: Arjun — est: 4d
- RED-3490 — feature flag + org-level default (pin-by-default for prod?) (2pts) — owner: PM — est: 2d

Notes / Implementation guidance (brief):
- Default for pin = OFF for new routes created via UI. Templates can be provided for "production" which set pin=ON and require typed confirmation.
- Analytics: fire events for pin_toggled, create_route(pinned), canary_started, promote_variant, rollback_variant. Tag events with org_id, route_id, variant_id.
- UX: prefer contextual inline explanations rather than one large help modal. Use microcopy and hover links to docs.
- Security: pin should not bypass access control. Only users with deploy/pin permissions can lock production routes.

Open questions (to resolve in grooming):
- Terminology: should we use "route" or "endpoint"? (Tradeoffs: endpoint = familiar; route = clearer for traffic split semantics)
- Should pin be sticky across rollouts for that route or per-variant only? (recommended: per-route pin; store pinned variant id)
- Default behavior for imported routes via API/terraform — should pins be preserved?
- Allow auto-upgrade campaigns (org-level) that can override unpinned routes — how to present opt-out flows?

Next steps / owners:
- Design: produce final copy variants and hi-fi mockups (Lena) — due: 2026-03-05
- Backend: spec API payload + migration plan for routes table (Arjun) — due: 2026-03-12
- Console: prototype header pill and pin confirmation modal (Marcus) — due: 2026-03-19
- PM: pick microcopy experiment variants and define A/B target metrics (Sofia) — due: 2026-03-01

Notes-to-self / quick brainstorm fragments (informal):
- consider adding a "safe-promo" button that will run a quick verification harness (a set of smoke prompts) before allowing promote from canary to full
- show a small timeline visual on the route details page for past rollouts and pin/unpin events
- add a policy that can auto-unpin after X days if flagged by org (maybe dangerous)

References and context links: RED-3371 (wireframe request), RED-3382 (pin modal), PR#5543 (initial backend API), confluence:Model Catalog Spec

-- end of working playback notes --

(If anything in here feels like it belongs in product-ops or in a separate security doc call it out. This is intentionally a working doc; keep comments inline.)
